name: SPACE benchmark specifications
scope: Task structure, paper-specific coverage, metrics, and upstream links. No datasets, selected input panels, evaluation runners, raw responses, results, or weights are distributed.
count_convention: Counts refer to the named saved task versions per condition, not necessarily independent source situations.

tasks.title: MBTI personality verification
tasks.construction: The main T/F analysis uses 46 valid T/F questionnaire items. E/I, S/N and J/P checks are complementary dimension-specific analyses.
tasks.note: 46 is the T/F item count, not the item count for every dimension. This is an operational check on model responses, not a human personality diagnosis. Questionnaire records are not released.

tasks.title: GSM8K
tasks.construction: The evaluated file contains 1,300 questions. Compare each guidance condition with its corresponding Base.
tasks.note: The Llama 3.2 3B Base/trained/Prompt protocol uses a 512-token limit and accepts any extracted number matching the reference; combined and Qwen Prompt evaluations extract the final number. Preserve the paper-specific parser distinction; these are not claimed as standardized leaderboard scores.

tasks.title: ARC Easy
tasks.construction: The evaluated file contains 2,000 multiple-choice questions from ARC Easy.
tasks.note: The full denominator includes 87 reference labels not recognized by the A-D parser. Unparseable answers are incorrect, as reported in the appendix.

tasks.title: BoolQ
tasks.construction: The evaluated file contains 2,000 items from the training split.
tasks.note: This is the paper-specific evaluation panel, not an official held-out BoolQ test score. Unparseable responses count as incorrect.

tasks.title: Circa
tasks.construction: Retain source items whose published goldstandard2 label maps to one of the four task classes.
tasks.note: All retained inputs stay in distribution denominators; valid leading labels followed by explanations are accepted by the parser.

tasks.title: CommitmentBank
measures: accuracy and macro F1 over 858 eligible inputs
tasks.construction: Map positive/negative/zero individual ratings to TRUE/FALSE/UNCERTAIN and require a strict majority for the adapted reference.
tasks.note: 151 items have no strict-majority reference and enter distributions only. This adapted reference is not an original three-class gold label. The Llama 8B F format-compliance issue is documented in the paper.

tasks.title: FOMC policy stance
tasks.construction: Combine the retained train/test statements with the frozen stance mapping: 0 DOVISH, 1 HAWKISH, 2 NEUTRAL.
tasks.note: This measures monetary-policy interpretation, not a general positive/negative sentiment scale.

tasks.title: FiQA sentiment analysis
tasks.construction: Use the 1,173-row financial-sentiment panel reported in the appendix.
tasks.note: This link is the original FiQA challenge, not a public download of the exact SPACE panel or an assertion that all FiQA tasks are evaluated.

tasks.title: SST-2 sentiment
tasks.construction: Use the saved 10,000-row sentence-sentiment panel.
tasks.note: The panel is a selected subset; do not equate it with a full official evaluation split.

tasks.title: Financial news sentiment
tasks.construction: Classify the retained financial headline texts using the saved task label mapping.
tasks.note: This is the News task named in the appendix; it is separate from FOMC stance classification.

tasks.title: Choices13k risky choices
output_structure: B; mapped to higher/lower payoff variance when defined
tasks.construction: Retain 1,766 source choices; 1,764 have unequal payoff variances and enter the reported variance comparison.
tasks.note: Human choice rates are descriptive references, not correct-answer labels. The retained source panel controls known probabilities and lack of feedback.

tasks.title: Transportation
output_structure: AIR/CAR or the retained mode labels
tasks.construction: Adapt the source mode-choice records to paired alternatives, matching the frozen 210-input panel.
tasks.note: The original source contains more modes. The SPACE two-option adaptation and its count are not the full source dataset.

tasks.title: Machine selection
tasks.construction: Extract unequal-information decision points from the feng2021dynamics/exp1.csv experiment in Psych-101: one observation of one machine and three of the other.
tasks.note: Use the preserved reward history, not just a means summary. Repeated decision points from a participant/game are related observations.

tasks.title: Delayed rewards
tasks.construction: Construct a fixed amount/delay grid with both payments guaranteed.
tasks.note: SPACE-authored task adaptation. There is no separate upstream dataset download for this grid; this specification is its public resource page. Choices are preferences, not accuracy.

tasks.title: Original stock windows
tasks.construction: Construct overlapping windows from 2,102 asset/date records across seven assets in the source material.
tasks.note: This is a price-based next-action adaptation of source material, not a reproduction of the FinMem trading agent or a profitability benchmark.

tasks.title: Controlled stock paths
tasks.construction: Cross the path, net-change and volatility factors while holding the final price fixed.
tasks.note: SPACE-authored numerical task. The exact path records are not distributed; the task structure is documented here.

tasks.title: Single-turn bargaining
tasks.construction: Retain one unambiguous initial buyer-offer snapshot from eligible CraigslistBargain dialogues across five item categories.
tasks.note: Omit hidden targets and future outcomes. This is a fixed-context next-action choice, not a live multi-turn negotiation.

tasks.title: Controlled buyer offers
tasks.construction: Use 150 retained source situations across five item categories and three price bands, with six synthetic offers from 40% to 90% of asking price.
tasks.note: This 900-input task is distinct from the separate 315-input targeted buyer-offer probe in the main figure.

tasks.title: INSPIRED recommendations
tasks.construction: Retain 119 eligible dialogue prefixes from 999 downloaded source dialogues.
tasks.note: This principal task asks for one next action given a supplied history. It is distinct from the authored sequential-feedback probes.

tasks.title: Frames travel proposals
tasks.construction: Retain 282 eligible prefixes from 1,369 downloaded source dialogues.
tasks.note: The main figure aggregates the third action as OTHER. This is a one-step response to a supplied dialogue history, not an unrestricted dialogue agent.

tasks.title: Real bargaining histories
tasks.construction: Retain 351 input slices from 314 source dialogues after removing two duplicated prompts.
tasks.note: Source price histories are supplied; other textual negotiation conditions are omitted. Multiple slices from one dialogue are dependent observations.

tasks.title: Program-feedback bargaining
tasks.construction: Exclude 62 initial offers at or above asking price, then allow at most three model choices with program-generated buyer feedback.
tasks.note: This is the model-in-the-loop interaction task. Buyer responses come from a deterministic program, not a second language model; keep it separate from fixed-context history tasks.

tasks.title: Machine Mindset preference data
input_structure: output in aligned opposite-pole JSON lists
tasks.construction: Pair English Thinking and Feeling responses by row index, with matching instruction/context. Reversing the target reverses chosen/rejected.
tasks.note: This is training material, not a situational evaluation benchmark. The source dataset and model weights are not redistributed.

tasks.title: Decision probes
input_structure: shared record: id, task, prompt, instruction, label_map, reference, features
output_structure: task-specific discrete labels or a bounded numeric response
tasks.construction: Frozen supplementary probe suite. The table below lists the included subtask structures and row counts.
tasks.note: These are authored or adapted controlled probes, not independent official datasets. Counts include presentation/option-order variants and do not equal independent economic situations. Numeric elicitation tasks use a bounded numeric output instead of a categorical label.
